subject: Hosted -> Dedicated: GPU tailoring & swap cadence proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan@velvetai.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring Dedicated commit — initial traffic profile and timing

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough Friday. We are close to a capacity decision and need a short technical attestation from Redwood so we can sign the reserved capacity paperwork. Specifically we need: 1) an initial right-sizing for steady-state qps and 95th p99 latency targets, 2) a proposed swap cadence (how often you recommend we run fleet swaps to move from hosted -> dedicated), and 3) a short list of pre-cutover validation checks VelvetAI must run.

Current footprint on hosted: ~4M tokens/day (mixed chat/generation), peaks at 650 rps for short bursts (1–2 min) during business hours, and a 60% tail of embedding calls to downstream indexing. We are targeting a go-live in early Jan if sizing checks look good. Can you get an initial proposal by next Monday?

Appreciate it — Jordan
Ops, VelvetAI

--
VelvetAI | ML-driven search for digital catalogs

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan@velvetai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated commit — initial traffic profile and timing

Jordan — thanks for the profile. We can absolutely produce a tailored sizing and a short swap cadence recommendation.

High-level ask from our side so our draft is precise:
- Confirm the percent of traffic that requires <250ms p99 vs. traffic that tolerates 500–800ms (this affects kernel selection and batching strategy).
- Provide a representative 30-min peak minute trace (timestamps + token counts) if you can — masked traces are fine.

Plan: we will deliver a one-page commitment estimate + a 2-week pre-cutover validation schedule by Monday (2026-12-07). Attached: a lightweight template we use for traces and a reference swap-cadence playbook.

Next steps: once you confirm the latency split I’ll assign Karthik to build the throughput model and Ben will produce the acceptance load profile for the on-prem GPUs.

Regards,
Maya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated commit — internal sizing plan

Team — draft checklist and modelling notes below (internal):

1) Ingest assumptions
- Baseline tokens/day: 4,000,000 (mixed)
- Burst window: 650 rps sustained for up to 120s, expected twice per day
- Embedding fraction: 60% calls are embeddings (lower CPU/GPU per call but higher throughput)

2) Model approach- Run throughput sim with two kernel profiles: low-latency (fp16 + KV cache aggressive) and cost-optimized (int8 + batching 32)
- Start with a 16xA10 equiv baseline per 1k rps for chat-heavy profile; adjust down for embedding-heavy workload (approx 1x A10 per 6k embedding rps)

3) Pre-cutover validation items (to hand to customer)
- Smoke: sanity requests (20 distinct prompts) at production token lengths
- Load: 3 ramp cycles to peak 1.2x expected burst (to check headroom)
- Cache priming: run typical user journeys to warm KV cache
- Failover: simulate region fallback to hosted variant

4) Swap cadence recommendation
- Weekly small swaps during day-of-week low usage for first 4 weeks, then biweekly for steady-state; maintenance can bundle minor kernel/quantization patches.

I’ll produce the numbers spreadsheet and a condensed narrative for Maya to send upstream. Ben — can you add the acceptance TPS targets for the embedding-heavy runs?

-Karthik

From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan@velvetai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated: VelvetAI sizing estimate + pre-cutover plan (draft)

Jordan — attaching our draft sizing estimate and a short pre-cutover checklist for your review. Key highlights in brief: 

- Steady-state recommended commit: 8 A10-equivalent GPUs for a mix workload (this maps to a 2x headroom over expected sustained qps with our default latency profile).
- Peak burst coverage: recommended autoscale buffer to reach 16 A10-equivalent for 90s bursts (or use dedicated burst pool).
- Embedding offload: we recommend routing embeddings to a quantized int8 pool to reduce cost; if VelvetAI prefers single pool, add +2 GPUs for headroom.
- Swap cadence: weekly 1–2 node swaps during low-usage windows for first 30 days; then move to 2-week cadence.

Attachments: velvetai_sizing_deltas_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with assumptions), swap-cadence-playbook-v3.pdf (playbook).

As discussed, we also propose a 10-day pre-cutover dry-run schedule — smoke, load, priming, and failover checks. If you approve these numbers we’ll convert them into the formal reserved capacity quote and an operations runbook.

Thanks,
Maya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan@velvetai.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@velvetai.com

Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated: VelvetAI sizing estimate + pre-cutover plan (draft)

Maya — this looks good, thanks. Two quick items: 1) can you document the rollback window and exact metrics we should watch during the 90s peak test? (p99 latency, CPU/gpu utilization thresholds), and 2) confirm whether the embedding int8 pool requires model conversion work on our side or if Redwood will handle conversion as part of the activation.

We have a procurement checkpoint on Thursday and need the formal quote + rollback criteria before EOD Wednesday. If you can get that, we’ll lock the Jan go-live target and route the contract.

Best — Jordan
